| `GET .../studies` | List the project's published studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}` | One study's full read: model, system prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environme
nt it publishes, and its insights envelope. The last two need workspace membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, ne
ver null |
> [!NOTE]
> **Swarms and User Testing are enabled per organization.** Everything in the
> four sections below is behind that gate, enforced server-side. If it is not
> on for your organization, the reads generally return empty and every **write**
> — creating a persona or goal, launching a run, publishing a study,
> requesting insights — answers `403` with a message naming the feature, not a
> `404` and not a validation error.
> Five operations are deliberately outside the gate, because every one of them
> *reduces* exposure and spend: cancelling a goal run, unpublishing a
> study, and archiving a persona, goal or swarm (each one's `DELETE`). An
> organization that loses access can still stop what is running and clean up
> what it authored.
> Ask us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) if you want it turned on.
**Swarms — authoring** (`/projects/{projectId}/personas...`, `.../goals...`,
`.../swarms...`) — the definitions a swarm run executes. A **persona** is a
reusable synthetic character; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a
**swarm** is an authoring container holding defaults for the goals made
under it. Nothing here starts anything — launching is
`POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs`.
| Endpoint | What it does |
| `GET .../personas` | List the project's personas |
| `POST .../personas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |
| `GET .../personas/{personaId}` | One persona |
| `PATCH .../personas/{personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so renaming is safe |
| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. **409** while goals still reference it |
| `GET .../goals` | List the project's goals |
| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` must be in this project |
| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |
| `PATCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `environmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |
| `DELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal — existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed |
| `GET .../swarms` | List swarm containers |
| `POST .../swarms` | Create a swarm container (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |
| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | One swarm |
| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update the container's defaults. Not a cascade — existing goals keep their own values |
| `DELETE .../swarms/{swarmId}` | **Archive** a swarm. The goals under it stay launchable |
**Swarms — generation** — drafts a model writes for you. Both routes return
candidates and **persist nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create
routes above. That is also why neither accepts an `Idempotency-Key` — a call
with no effect has nothing to de-duplicate, and offering one would imply the
drafts are stable across retries when they are not.
| Endpoint | What it does |
| `POST .../personas/generate` | Draft a slate of personas (and goals for each) grounded in a server attachment or an environment
| `POST .../goals/generate` | Draft goals for a persona passed **by value**, so you can draft before you save |
> [!WARNING]
> The generation routes consume **no customer credits** — the model cost is on
> MCPJam. They are still subject to usage limits, and each limit means a
> different wait: a per-minute burst brake (`429`, retry in seconds), your
